en.html:
In the detention center, boredom is the ruling authority. Its administration is very thorough.

Prison is a different arrangement. There, the sentence has already been decided. Here they keep prisoners awaiting judgment, and the condemned, who are treated as though still awaiting it. The condemned man's punishment is death, at the end. Nothing extra is to be supplied beforehand. Accordingly, no forced labor.

On paper one may volunteer for work. In this Kanto Detention Center, however, the necessary arrangements have not been made. Permission is fully available; the permitted thing is unavailable. This was the guard's explanation.

Outside exercise: thirty minutes per day. Bas. For every remaining minute, please enjoy the inside of the cell quietly.

Reading and writing are allowed, with restrictions. A long day will not die from such small attacks.

Two options remain. Sleep and sleep. Or, if the gradual ruin of one's mind and body from excessive sleep is not acceptable, exercise within slightly more than two tatami of space.

Noise is forbidden, naturally. Equipment also, even if made from things already inside the cell. Depending on the guard, rubbing oneself with a dry towel is preparation for strangulation. The towel may be innocent. That is not sufficient.

Practice swings are out of the question. Martial forms merely exercise the guards' already damaged nerves. In the end, push-ups, sit-ups, back extensions. Standard muscle training, with no suspicious imagination involved.

Which is exactly what I was doing.

ja.html:
拘置所の一日は退屈によって支配される。

　既に刑の確定した者のための施設である刑務所とは
異なり、拘置所に収容されるのは未決囚と未決囚扱い
の死刑囚（彼らに与えられるべき刑罰は最後の死のみ
であり、他には無い）なので、強制労働は行われない。

　規定の上では志願すれば労役に就くことも可能な筈
だが、この関東拘置所はその体制が整っていないため、
要望に応えることは不可能――とのことだった。
　看守からそう聞いている。

　外に出て体を動かせるのは一日あたり三十分間だけ。
　他の時間は全て独房内で静かに過ごさねばならない。

　読書や書き物は可能だが、制限がつく。
　長い一日を潰すのは無理だ。

　となれば後は、ひたすらに寝て過ごすか、あるいは
――貪眠による心身機能の低下を受容できないのなら
ば――二畳余の空間で許される限りの運動を行うしか
ない。

　派手な音を立てる行為は当然、認められない。
　器具を使うような運動も無論――例え獄室内にある
物で間に合わせるとしても。乾布摩擦でさえ、看守に
よっては絞殺の準備とみられる。

　素振りなどは論外。体術の型なども看守のささくれ
立った神経をいたずらに刺激するのみだ。
　結局のところ、出来ることは腕立て、腹筋、背筋と
いったスタンダードな筋トレの類に限られる。

　つまりは、俺が今している事もそれなのだった。

en.html:
Kageaki"Ji."
Jailer"Orders have come. Temporary transfer to Kamakura Police Station for questioning. The car is here already. Get ready within ten minutes."
Kageaki"Understood."
Jailer"...One thing, though. You."
Kageaki"Yes?"
Jailer"What were you doing just now?"
Kageaki"Push-ups."
Jailer"...Achha. Push-ups, it seems."
Kageaki"Yes."
Jailer"Where were you born?"
Kageaki"Nagasaki."
Jailer"I am from Akita."
Kageaki"Very good kiritanpo, I hear."
Jailer"Nagasaki, champon, na."
Kageaki"Yes."
Jailer"...In my hometown, for push-ups, both hands AND both feet go on the ground. That is our local custom."
Kageaki"Most places, I believe."
Jailer"Push-ups with the feet floating. First time in my life I am seeing this arrangement."
Kageaki"From other people, I have also hardly seen it."
Jailer"Does it not hurt?"
Kageaki"I suffer and writhe. Fully."
Jailer"...Achha. That is a relief."
Kageaki"Glad my suffering could be of assistance."
Jailer"Get ready, please."
Kageaki"Ji."

景明「はい」
看守「事情聴取のため、お前を一時的に鎌倉署へ 移送するとの通達があった。迎えの車はもう 来ている。 　一〇分以内に支度をしろ」
景明「わかりました」
看守「……ところで、お前」
景明「何でしょうか」
看守「今、何をしていた？」
景明「腕立て伏せです」
看守「……そうか。 　腕立て伏せか」
景明「はい」
看守「お前、生まれは？」
景明「長崎です」
看守「俺は秋田だ」
景明「きりたんぽが美味しいとか」
看守「長崎は、ちゃんぽんだな」
景明「ええ」
看守「……俺の故郷では、腕立て伏せってのは、 両手と両足を地面につけてやるもんだった」
景明「大概は、そうでしょう」
看守「足を浮かせてやる腕立て伏せっていうのは 初めて見た」
景明「自分も、他人がやるのはあまり見た覚えが ありません」
看守「苦しくないのか？」
景明「苦しみ悶えます」
看守「…………そうか。 　安心したよ」
景明「それは幸いです」
看守「支度をしてくれ」
景明「はい」

I take the tea bowl from the table. A faint fragrance tickles my nose: new tea from Enshu. The color admits that it was cheap. On quality, though, there is no shameful confession to make.

I tilt the bowl just enough for the surface to meet my lips, and wet the tip of my tongue.

Kageaki"Muramasa's view is the same. Rather... not even one person escaped. Total annihilation, with nothing left over for the word to exaggerate. Misunderstanding is not possible."
Chief"Correct. In military language, annihilation means enough losses to destroy a unit's ability to function. Thirty to forty percent, roughly."
Chief"Annihilated, and sixty percent still alive. Normal usage. But encounter that thing, and the sixty percent are also refused."
Kageaki"Because this is not war. Between perpetrator and victim, there is no negotiation called combat. Compared with this, fighting is a mild little game."
Kageaki"A natural disaster, bas. A great tsunami upon a coastal village. A great eruption upon a village below the mountain. Where is the permission for survivors in that?"

en.html:
The facts I state as facts. No reply comes.

On the east wall of this not particularly large room hangs one painting. Mulberry cultivation. An ordinary landscape, showing no dangerous ambition in technique either. But if asked whether I like it: yes.

No famous artist made it. No artist at all, in fact. The owner of the room painted it himself. Perhaps because it is so ordinary, looking at it settles the mind. ...Or perhaps I am giving marks for knowing the painter.

This is the entire decoration of the room. Everything else is practical furniture, documents in quantity, assorted objects from which all taste and charm have been successfully excluded.

For the chief of the police entrusted with Kamakura's peace—supposed to be entrusted, let us keep that qualification—the surroundings are rather sorry. If I put a little effort into my sarcasm, I could promote them to deplorable.

Or realistic, perhaps.

In the realistic office, the realistic chief takes his eyes off the table's wood grain and looks at me again.

ja.html:
事実を事実として言い切る。
　返答はなかった。

　広くもない室内の東側の壁に、絵が一幅、飾られて
いる。桑の栽培の様子を描いた、ごくごく平凡な風景
画だ。技術的にも見るべき点は特にないだろう。
　だが好悪を問うなら、好みだった。

　著名人の作品ではない。いや、画家の手になるもの
でさえない。それはこの部屋の主の、自筆だった。
　凡庸な作品だからこそと言うべきか、見る人を落ち
着かせるような趣がある。……贔屓目かもしれないが。

　そんな絵だけが、この部屋にあって唯一、装飾品と
呼べるものだった。
　後は実用本位の家具と多くの資料類、味も素っ気も
ない諸々があるばかりだ。

　鎌倉市の治安を預かる――べき――警察署の首長が
座すにしては、寂しい佇まいだと言えた。
　もう少し皮肉な表現力を駆使するなら、<ruby>嘆かわしい<rt>・・・・・</rt></ruby>
佇まいだと評することも可能かもしれない。

　あるいは<ruby>現実的<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>か。
　現実的な署長室の現実的な警察署長は、テーブルの
木目に向けていた視線を外し、再びこちらを見やって
いる。

en.html:
Chief"The 'egg.' You prevented it from hatching?"
Kageaki"Yes. Ukyo Nagasaka, the Rokuhara magistrate, and his mercenary Kotaro Fuma. Confirmed both as hosts, killed both."
Chief"For the present, that is the most important thing. That horror must not start multiplying also."
Chief"You have suffered much for this. Good work."
Kageaki"No. The suffering was certainly not mine."
Chief"...Any information about Silver Star?"
Kageaki"From Ukyo Nagasaka, nothing. Kotaro Fuma appears to have spoken with it, at least. Useful information, however—its whereabouts, for example—nothing from him either."
Chief"Hm. Somebody, somewhere, is sheltering it. That is the conclusion we should draw, but..."
Kageaki"Without that, the reasoning will not stand."
Chief"Nationwide search, listed as a missing person, and not one result. Insufficient police strength may explain some of it..."
Chief"But two years now. There must be support."
Kageaki"Agreed. The purpose, though, I cannot understand at all. A killer who harms everyone. Who is helping, and for what happiness?"
Chief"Haan. No sense in it, is there? ...Unfortunately, the world does a great deal of business without consulting sense."
Kageaki"Then logical deduction alone will have difficulty reaching the truth. The truth is not cooperating."
Chief"Exactly. Sit in a comfortable chair and become a great detective—the chair will benefit, that is all."
Chief"We need decisive information. Sorry, Kageaki. I must ask it of you."
Kageaki"I understand. Apart from that, one matter is troubling me."
Chief"What matter?"
Kageaki"The man who supplied Kotaro Fuma's tsurugi. Ichizo Sorimachi. Member of the Nogiyama Group, in Rokuhara's employ, and GHQ's errand man also."
Chief"Ah..."
Kageaki"Assuming I swallow everything I was told, without chewing: GHQ confiscated Fuma's tsurugi, and Sorimachi arranged its return. Why was that allowed?"
Kageaki"What GHQ collected in its tsurugi hunt should surely be under strict seal. Otherwise, why spend all that effort hunting them down? Collect with one hand, distribute with the other?"
Chief"...That teacher. Ryoubu Suzukawa. His tsurugi came from an unknown source also, didn't it?"
Kageaki"Yes. There may be a connection."
Chief"Your view?"
Kageaki"...For a reasonable-looking explanation: GHQ has no interest in Yamato. Occupation Army discipline becomes lax. Diverting supplies becomes easy. Something along those lines."
Chief"And how many marks do you give your own answer?"
Kageaki"Fail."
Chief"Why?"
Kageaki"Does GHQ have no interest in Yamato?"
Chief"No. ...Haan. There only, the answer falls down."
Chief"I already have a suspicion about this. Tomorrow we will discuss it. It will come up anyway, and this is not a subject I want passing through my mouth repeatedly."
Kageaki"Tomorrow?"
Chief"Stay at my official residence tonight. No need to return to detention. Tomorrow, after work, there is somewhere I want you to come with me."
Kageaki"Where?"
Chief"Hachimangu. His Imperial Highness wishes to meet you."
Kageaki"..."
Kageaki"And why would that be?"
Chief"His Highness is more concerned about you than you realize. Silver Star has harmed so many citizens; he takes the matter as his own."
Chief"His hopes for you are considerable. For some time he has been asking to speak with you personally."
Kageaki"But this body is polluted with blood. To bring it before a member of the imperial family—"
Chief"He is not the sort to fuss over these trifles."
Kageaki"I cannot call it a trifle. Those who preside over the altars of the state should keep impurity at a distance."
Chief"Arre, don't start. His Highness is practical, that is the point. He wants to hear the actual situation from someone on the spot. Meaning you. Who else?"
Chief"Bas, that much. No charm is required from your side. Answer his questions about the case. Job finished."
Chief"Not quite one hour of suffering. Manage that much and come."
Kageaki"...Understood."

Who is helping, and for what happiness?"Chief"Haan. No sense in it, is there? ...Unfortunately, the world does a great deal of business without consulting sense."Kageaki"Then logical deduction alone will have difficulty reaching the truth. The truth is not cooperating."Chief"Exactly. Sit in a comfortable chair and become a great detective—the chair will benefit, that is all."Chief"We need decisive information. Sorry, Kageaki. I must ask it of you."Kageaki"I understand. Apart from that, one matter is troubling me."Chief"What matter?"Kageaki"The man who supplied Kotaro Fuma's tsurugi. Ichizo Sorimachi. Member of the Nogiyama Group, in Rokuhara's employ, and GHQ's errand man also."Chief"Ah..."Kageaki"Assuming I swallow everything I was told, without chewing: GHQ confiscated Fuma's tsurugi, and Sorimachi arranged its return. Why was that allowed?"Kageaki"What GHQ collected in its tsurugi hunt should surely be under strict seal. Otherwise, why spend all that effort hunting them down? Collect with one hand, distribute with the other?"Chief"...That teacher. Ryoubu Suzukawa. His tsurugi came from an unknown source also, didn't it?"Kageaki"Yes. There may be a connection."Chief"Your view?"Kageaki"...For a reasonable-looking explanation: GHQ has no interest in Yamato. Occupation Army discipline becomes lax. Diverting supplies becomes easy. Something along those lines."Chief"And how many marks do you give your own answer?"Kageaki"Fail."Chief"Why?"Kageaki"Does GHQ have no interest in Yamato?"Chief"No. ...Haan. There only, the answer falls down."Chief"I already have a suspicion about this. Tomorrow we will discuss it. It will come up anyway, and this is not a subject I want passing through my mouth repeatedly."Kageaki"Tomorrow?"Chief"Stay at my official residence tonight. No need to return to detention. Tomorrow, after work, there is somewhere I want you to come with me."Kageaki"Where?"Chief"Hachimangu. His Imperial Highness wishes to meet you."Kageaki"..."Kageaki"And why would that be?"Chief"His Highness is more concerned about you than you realize. Silver Star has harmed so many citizens; he takes the matter as his own."Chief"His hopes for you are considerable. For some time he has been asking to speak with you personally."Kageaki"But this body is polluted with blood. To bring it before a member of the imperial family—"Chief"He is not the sort to fuss over these trifles."Kageaki"I cannot call it a trifle. Those who preside over the altars of the state should keep impurity at a distance."Chief"Arre, don't start. His Highness is practical, that is the point. He wants to hear the actual situation from someone on the spot. Meaning you. Who else?"Chief"Bas, that much. No charm is required from your side. Answer his questions about the case. Job finished."Chief"Not quite one hour of suffering. Manage that much and come."Kageaki"...Understood."

署長「〝卵〟の孵化は阻止したのだな」
景明「はい。 　六波羅代官長坂右京とその傭兵風魔小太郎 が寄生体であることを確認、両名を殺害しま した」
署長「現状で何よりも肝要なのはそこだ。 　あんなものに増え・・られては堪らん」
署長「御苦労だったな」
景明「いいえ。 　苦しんだのは決して、自分ではありません から」
署長「…………。 　銀星号について情報は得られたか？」
景明「長坂右京からは何も。 　風魔小太郎の方はあれ・・と会話程度の接触は した様子ですが、所在などの有意義な情報は やはり得られませんでした」
署長「そうか。 　あれは何処かに、何者かが、保護・・している とみるべきなのだが……」
景明「そう考えなくては、理屈に合いません」
署長「失踪者扱いで全国に捜索を手配しているに も拘わらず、まるで引っ掛からないのだから な。 　警察力の不足もあるだろうが……」
署長「もう二年にもなる。 　支援者がいると考えるべきだ」
景明「全くに。しかし、目的が皆目わかりません。 　誰もを害する殺戮者に、誰がどうして手を 貸すのか」
署長「ああ。筋道が通らんな？ 　……そして世の中、筋道の通らん話が割合 横行するから困る」
景明「であれば、論理的推察のみによって真実へ 近付くのは難しいという事になります」
署長「その通りだ。 　安楽椅子の探偵を気取っていてもどうにも ならん」
署長「決定的な情報が要る。 　済まないが宜しく頼むぞ、景明」
景明「承知しています。 　ところで。それとは別件で一つ、気になる 事柄が」
署長「なんだ？」
景明「風魔小太郎に劔冑を提供した男です。 　名は雪車町一蔵。六波羅御雇の野木山組に 属し、且つＧＨＱの御用聞きでもある」
署長「ああ……」
景明「自分が聞かされた話をすべて鵜呑みにする なら、という前提ですが――風魔はＧＨＱに 奪われた劔冑を雪車町の手配りで取り戻して いる。何故、そのような真似が許されたのか」
景明「ＧＨＱの〝劔冑狩り〟政策の成果は当然、 厳重に封印されている筈。 　でなければ、手間隙を費やして劔冑を狩り 集めた意味がありません」
署長「…………。 　先日の教師。鈴川令法か。彼も出所不明の 劔冑を持っていたのだったな」
景明「はい。 　関連性が疑われます」
署長「お前はどう考えている？」
景明「……妥当な推論をするなら。 　ＧＨＱの大和への無関心が進駐軍の綱紀を 緩ませ、物資の横流しを安易に行わせている ――というあたりでしょう」
署長「その推論に対する自己採点は？」
景明「不可」
署長「なぜ？」
景明「ＧＨＱは大和に無関心ですか？」
署長「否。 　……そう、そういうことだな」
署長「この件については既に推測を持っている。 　だが、明日話そう。どうせ話題になる…… こんな話は幾度も口にしたくない」
景明「明日？」
署長「今日は私の役宅で休んでおけ。拘置所には 戻らなくていい。 　明日、仕事が済んだ後で付き合って欲しい 所がある」
景明「どちらへ」
署長「八幡宮だ。 　親王殿下がお前に会いたがっておられる」
景明「…………」
景明「それはまた、何故」
署長「お前が思っている以上に、殿下はお前の事 を気に掛けておられるよ。 　殿下は国民を多く害する銀星号事件を我が 身の事として考えておいでだ」
署長「お前にかける期待も大きい。 　一度親しく言葉を交わしたいと、実は前々 から仰せであった」
景明「しかし。 　血の穢れに塗れた身を皇族の御前には――」
署長「そんなつまらん事にこだわられる殿下では ない」
景明「つまらぬ事とは思われません。 　社稷を司る者は不浄を遠ざけるべき」
署長「まあ、そう言うな。 　要は実際的な方なのだよ、殿下は。事件の 実情を知るために現場の者の声を聞きたいと 望んでおられる。となればお前しかいない」
署長「それだけだ。だから別に、愛想を振りまく 必要もない。 　事件について殿下の御下問にお答えすれば 済む」
署長「小一時間ほどの辛抱だ。我慢して付き合え」
景明「……わかりました」

en.html:
I nod. What else to do? A heavy prospect, but once he puts it like this, my refusal has no legs to stand on.

The prince at Hachimangu. Rumor calls him the imperial family's oddity. Apparently rumor has done its work correctly, possibly even shown restraint. A nobleman wanting to meet a prisoner. This is a new variety for me.

...Let him not dig into every little thing, that is all I ask.

I drain the bowl. No steam remains. Without its warmth, the tea has become bitter beyond all necessity.

やむなく首肯する。
　気の重い話だが、そう言われては仕方がなかった。

　――八幡宮の親王。
　皇室の変わり種という風評はこれまでにも耳にして
いたが、どうやら噂通りあるいは噂以上の人物らしい。
　獄囚に会いたがる貴人など聞いたこともない。

　……あまり根掘り葉掘りあれこれと聞かれなければ
良いが。

　既に湯気など立てない茶碗を呷る。
　温かみを失った茶は無闇に苦かった。

en.html:
Out through the staff gate of Kamakura Police Station, onto the street.

The chief has come personally to see me off. His kindness I appreciate. The possible spectators, less so. Police chief bidding farewell to detention prisoner: the picture is not a normal one.

Then again, he is wearing a police uniform; I am not wearing prison clothes. Nobody has been supplied with my side of the picture. I know this worry is unnecessary. Still, I am doing it properly.

職員用の通用門から鎌倉署の外へ。
　通りへ出る。

　署長はわざわざ見送りをしてくれた。厚情は有難い
が、人目を思って気に病みもする。
　警察署長が拘置囚を送っているのだから異様な図だ。

　とはいえ署長は警察の制服姿だが、こちらは拘置所
の囚人服を着ているわけではない。
　無用の心配だとはわかっていた。

en.html:
The chief's gaze moves suddenly. Behind me, to the right at an angle.

I follow it.

Someone is there.

Back against the concrete wall, head a little lowered, watching us sideways. On the surface, no particular interest. Inside the eyes, fierce determination. The surface is giving very poor information.

As far as I know, she has always been like this.

That face is firmly printed in my memory. To recall her full name, no effort is required.

署長の視線がふと、泳ぐ。
　俺の後方、斜め右側へ。

　つられて追う。
　
　人影があった。

　コンクリート塀に背を預け、こちらをうつむき加減
の横目で窺っている。
　一見、何の気もなさそうな素ぶり。しかしその実、
眼球の奥には激しい意志の光があった。

　俺の知る限り、彼女がいつもそうであったように。

　脳裏に強く記憶されている顔だった。
　姓名を思い出すのに何の苦労もいらない。
